params.body:
## What

An editor can pin one post as the lead of gentells.com. The pipeline sends `featured_at` with that post; the site stores it and puts the pinned post first where a page leads with one post:

- the member home: the pinned post in the featured slot, the six newest under it
- the visitor home: the pinned post first, then the two newest
- `/posts`: the pinned post in the featured slot when the filter kept it

Without a pin nothing changes: the newest post leads.

## Why

The lead was always the most recently published post, so the only way to put a stronger piece on top was to publish it later. Curate in the Studio now arranges the front page, and the lead is the one post placement that matters most.

## How

- Migration: nullable `featured_at` on `articles`, cast as a datetime.
- `Projection::upsertArticle` stores `featured_at` from the payload, so a pin and an unpin both arrive with the article's next update.
- `Article::scopeLeadFirst`: the pinned post first, then by publication. `scopePublished` is unchanged on purpose: the open window counts the fifteen most recent by publication, and a pin must not reopen an old post.

## Tests

`PinnedLeadTest`: the newest leads without a pin; the pinned post leads the member home, comes first on the visitor home and takes the featured slot on `/posts`; a pin does not reopen an old post; the projection stores and clears the pin.

Full suite locally: 429 of 430 pass. The one failure is `BuildStampTest`, which reads the checkout's `.git` directory and returns 404 in a git worktree; it does not touch this change. Pint passes.

## Depends on

The pipeline change that sends `featured_at` (the Curate front page). Until that is deployed every post arrives with `featured_at` null and the site behaves exactly as today, so this can merge first.
params.title: Let an editor pin the lead post
